_comment: Owner-approved exceptions to the agent file-ownership scope guard in backend/tests/test_trusted_context_shadow_wireup.py. Read from BASE only, and only for content the grant names: a branch can neither write itself a grant nor reuse an existing one for a different change. Same conventions as intelligence_exceptions.json beside it. This registry does not replace or relax the intelligence_exceptions / GOV-002 requirements; both apply.

_entry_shape.exception_id: stable id, referenced by the PR that uses it
exact_file_scope: one exact repository path per entry; never patterns
_entry_shape.base_content_sha256: sha256 of the committed BASE blob BEFORE the approved change
authorized_content_sha256: one sha256 of the committed HEAD blob AFTER the approved change
_entry_shape.task_scope: what the change is for, in prose, for a human reader
_entry_shape.owner_approval_ref: https link to the owner's approval
_entry_shape.expires_at: YYYY-MM-DD; a date the guard cannot parse is refused

_pending.note: The welcome-coupon economics grant for backend/services/coupon_generator.py is approved (see owner_approval_ref) but cannot be written yet: authorized_content_sha256 is derived from the implementation diff, which does not exist. It is added as a one-line entry once that diff is presented for review. Until then this registry grants nothing, which is what an empty exceptions list means.

_awaiting_owner_approval.note: Complete entries proposed for the owner's decision. They grant nothing: the guard reads only "exceptions", and only from BASE. On the owner's approval an entry moves into "exceptions" unchanged except for owner_approval_ref, which becomes the https link to that approval, in its own reviewed commit. An entry the owner declines is removed. A change to either blob after an entry was written invalidates its digests, and a new entry is proposed instead.

exceptions.task_scope: PR #1145, commerce runtime catalogue pagination. One total catalogue search order (in_stock DESC, id) on every search path: the full-text path returns rows in the order it selected them instead of heap order, and the ILIKE and Arabic-normalised paths gain id as the tie-breaker. One shared search strategy (_search_steps) for the existing row search and a new ids-only candidate read (search_product_candidates, reading cap+1 to prove exhaustion), plus get_by_ids and top_product_candidates for the general browse. Match predicates, limits and callers are unchanged; the order of the rows every existing caller receives, and which of several tied rows a limit keeps, become deterministic.
